title: mu settings
description: Judges, decision points, features, models and context. The mu command line uses the same settings.
applyNote: Changes apply to new conversations. A running conversation keeps the settings it started with until you reconnect it.
keyHelp: After you save the key, it isn't shown again. It stays on this computer, readable only by your user account.
keyKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved key
endpointRule: Enter an address that starts with https:// or http://. It can't include a user name, password, query or fragment.
endpointPlain: This address uses plain http, so the key and your messages aren't encrypted. That's fine for a server on this computer or your own network, even one you reach through a name in your hosts file. Use https over the internet.

harness.tooOld: This version of mu is too old to list its decision points and features. Update mu to see them here. Basic settings still work.
harness.unsupported: mu describes its settings in a format this app doesn't recognize (version {{version}}). Update the app to edit decision points and features.

save.saved: Saved. New conversations use these settings; reconnect running ones to apply them.
save.stale: The settings changed after this page loaded them (from the mu command line or a running conversation), so nothing was saved. Reload to see the current settings. Your unsaved edits will be lost.

options.emptyText: Leave empty to use the default
options.addNumber: Type a number and press Enter

problem.type: This value has the wrong type.
problem.range: This value is outside the allowed range.
problem.choice: This isn't one of the allowed values.
problem.length: Too long, or an entry is empty.

features.lead: What mu does for you in the background. Turn a feature off and mu stops doing it.
features.boardModelElsewhere: To choose the model that writes the board, go to Board model.
features.noOptions: This feature has no other settings.
features.noSuchFeature: This version of mu doesn't have this feature.

judges.tiersHelp: mu asks the judges in order. A judge only sees the questions earlier judges weren't sure about.
judges.orderHelp: The first judge is the one you chose on the Judges page.
judges.firstTier: The judge you chose on the Judges page. Set its service, address and key there.

auto.name: Automatic
auto.help: Uses the first service that has a key, in this order: TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, OpenCode Zen, Cloudflare. With no key set, Jev 1.13 runs on OpenCode Zen, free for a limited time. OpenCode receives what Jev judges and doesn't train on it.

opencodeFree.name: OpenCode Zen (free)
opencodeFree.help: Jev 1.13 on OpenCode Zen, free for a limited time. No key or account needed. OpenCode doesn't train on what Jev reads.

openrouter.name: OpenRouter
openrouter.help: Always connects through OpenRouter, with an OpenRouter API key. This key is used only for Jev; it doesn't change the key for OpenRouter's chat models.

gateway.name: Vercel AI Gateway
gateway.help: Always connects through the Vercel AI Gateway.

opencode.name: OpenCode Zen
opencode.help: Jev 1.13 on OpenCode Zen, billed per call to your OpenCode account. The same key also unlocks OpenCode Zen's chat models in mu.

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
cloudflare.help: Jev on Cloudflare Workers AI, with a Cloudflare API token and your account ID.
cloudflare.accountHelp: Find it on the Workers AI page of the Cloudflare dashboard. It's stored the same way as the token.

custom.name: Custom service
custom.help: Any service that supports TypeSafe's System One protocol: one you run yourself, a relay on your network or another Jev provider.

judges.baseUrlHelp: Leave empty to use TypeSafe's default address.
judges.customUrlHelp: The service's System One address. Its key is sent only to this address.
judges.customTier: A judge you added yourself. Change it in mu's settings file.

types.clmHelp: Runs on your own CLM server.
types.classifierHelp: A classifier model from mu's model catalog: {{model}}. mu calls it with its provider's key.

judges.intro: While it works, mu has many small questions to settle: how to handle a message, or whether a step breaks a rule you set. Choose the judge that answers them.
judges.modeHelp: On: the judge's verdicts take effect. Off: every step runs as usual. Decision points without their own setting follow this one.
judges.custom: Your first judge is a custom one. View or change it on the Judge order page.

jev.title: Jev
jev.description: TypeSafe's hosted judge model. Fast and accurate. Free on OpenCode Zen for a limited time, or pay per call with a key for TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, OpenCode Zen, Cloudflare or your own service.

local.title: Local Laya
local.description: Runs on this computer with no network and no cost. Good at classifying; less reliable at matching related items and at scoring.

clm.title: CLM
clm.description: Answers the same questions as Jev, on your own server (clm-serve). Its encoder needs a GPU; there's no per-call cost.

laya.stopped: Installed but not running. mu starts it when needed.
laya.platform: Laya can't run on this computer. It needs Windows or Linux (x64 or arm64), or a Mac with Apple silicon.
laya.needsUv: Installing Laya requires uv, a Python package manager. Install uv, then come back here.
laya.confirmText: This downloads about {{size}} MB of Python packages and model weights from PyPI and Hugging Face into mu's folder, and takes a few minutes. Laya starts once it's installed.

onnx.missing: Laya's model isn't on this computer yet (about {{size}} MB). mu doesn't download it for you: get the files from Hugging Face, put them in the model folder, then click Check and start.
onnx.stopped: The model is in place, but Laya isn't running. When Laya is your judge, mu starts it automatically when the app opens.
onnx.starting: Checking the model and starting Laya. The first check reads the whole model, so it takes a moment.
onnx.wrongFiles: These files don't match the version mu was tested with. Download them again: {{files}}
onnx.command: With the Hugging Face CLI (hf), this command downloads everything:

problem.wrong: Some model files don't match the version mu was tested with. Download them again.
problem.runtime: This computer couldn't run the model.
problem.port: Another program is already using Laya's port ({{port}}).
problem.stopped: Laya stopped before it was ready.
problem.foreign: A copy of Laya that mu didn't start is already running. Stop it from wherever it was started.

clm.addressHelp: Where clm-serve listens, such as http://192.168.1.20:8700. Leave empty for this computer ({{address}}).
clm.keyPlaceholder: Only if the server requires one
clm.keyHelp: Only needed if the server was started with CLM_API_KEY. Enter the same value. After you save the key, it isn't shown again.
clm.unmeasured: CLM's accuracy on mu's decisions hasn't been measured yet.

status.down: Nothing is responding at {{address}}. Start clm-serve there, or fix the address.
status.encoderDown: The server responds, but its encoder doesn't. Every question fails until its embedding server (vLLM) is running.
status.model: The server doesn't serve {{model}}. It serves {{models}}.
status.keyNeeded: The server requires a key. Enter the one it was started with (CLM_API_KEY).
status.keySaved: The server requires a key, and one is saved.
status.mock: This server runs CLM's mock encoder, so its answers are noise, not real CLM verdicts.

context.autoHelp: Compacts the conversation history when the context window is nearly full.
context.limitHelp: 0 uses the model's context window minus the reserve. Otherwise, {{min}} to {{max}}. Checked before each model request; it's not a hard cutoff.
context.limitProblem: Use 0, or a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
context.lead: When to compact a conversation, how large its context can grow and which features work on it.

full.title: Full access
full.description: Runs everything without asking. Anything you've told mu not to do is still blocked.

judge.title: Judge mode
judge.description: Reads and edits inside the project go ahead. The judge decides on commands, changes outside the project and actions outside this computer, and asks you only when it's unsure.

ask.title: Ask first
ask.description: Only reads go ahead. mu asks you before every edit, command and action outside this computer.

kind.edit: mu wants to edit a file
kind.shell: mu wants to run a command
kind.run: mu wants to run a program
kind.outside: mu wants to change a file outside the project
kind.other: mu wants to take an action outside this computer

reason.ask: Ask first: mu asks you before every edit, command and action outside this computer.
reason.unsure: The judge isn't sure this step is what you want.
reason.beyond: The judge thinks this goes beyond what you asked for.
reason.unrelated: The judge thinks this isn't part of the task.
reason.protected: This touches mu's own settings; only you can allow it.
reason.nojudge: No judge is available yet, so mu asks you about each step.
reason.judgedown: The judge didn't answer this time, so mu is asking you.

providers.lead: Where your models come from: subscriptions and endpoints. Pick a conversation's model and thinking level in its message box.
providers.title: Providers
providers.name: Display name
providers.idHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Can't be changed after you save.

idProblem.format: Use up to 40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit.
idProblem.reserved: This ID belongs to a built-in provider. Using it would reroute that provider instead of adding a new one.
idProblem.taken: This ID is already in use.

providers.keyReplace: A key set by hand in models.json is in use. Entering a key here replaces it.
providers.authHeader: Also send Authorization: Bearer (some proxies need it)
providers.headers: Custom headers from models.json are kept as is: {{names}}. Their values may be secret, so this page doesn't show them: edit them in models.json.
providers.pick: Choose a provider on the left, or add one.
providers.foreignHelp: This entry reroutes a built-in provider or uses an API format this page can't edit. You can remove it here; to change it, edit models.json.
providers.builtinHelp: mu reported this provider as available the last time it connected, usually because its API key is set in your environment. To remove it, delete that key from the environment; it disappears the next time mu connects.
providers.unreadable: Couldn't read models.json, so providers can't be shown or saved. Fix the file by hand, then reload.
providers.commented: models.json contains comments, and saving from here would remove them, so providers are read-only. Remove the comments by hand to edit providers here.
providers.summary: Sign in with a subscription and use it right away, or connect any OpenAI-, Anthropic- or Gemini-compatible endpoint.
providers.removeSaved: When you save, it's deleted from models.json along with its stored key.
providers.removeUnsaved: It hasn't been saved, so anything you entered here is discarded.
providers.removeEntry: When you save, this manual entry is deleted from models.json. If it overrides a built-in provider, that provider reverts to its defaults.
providers.removeDefault: It's the default for new conversations, so the default model is cleared too.

defaults.summary: What new conversations start with. You can still switch within a conversation.
defaults.levelHelp: Levels this model doesn't support are disabled.
defaults.levelClamped: Not set means Medium. If the model doesn't support a level, mu uses the nearest one it does.
defaults.noReasoning: This model doesn't support thinking, so conversations with it always start with thinking off.

accounts.signOutConfirm: Sign out of {{name}}? You'll need to sign in again to use it.
accounts.instant: Signing in or out takes effect immediately. No need to save.
accounts.byKeyHelp: You're not signed in with a subscription, but mu reported this provider as available the last time it connected, usually because its API key is set in your environment. Signing in switches it to the subscription.
accounts.otherRunning: {{name}} sign-in is in progress. Only one sign-in can run at a time.

intro.title: Welcome to mu
intro.lead: mu is a coding agent that does the work: it reads your project, edits code, runs commands and tests, and keeps going until the job is done.

judge.title: A check at every step
judge.text: A built-in judge watches the key moments, so mu thinks before it acts, follows your rules and checks its work before calling a job done.

control.title: You see it, you steer it
control.text: Checkpoints let you roll back changes. When mu uses the in-app browser, you can watch each step and pause or take over.

ready.title: Works out of the box
ready.text: It picks up the rules, skills and MCP servers you've already set up in Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.

login.waiting: The {{name}} sign-in page is open in your browser. Sign in and allow access; this page continues automatically.
login.codePlaceholder: Paste the code shown in your browser, or the URL it ended on

login.waitingDevice: The {{name}} verification page is open in your browser. Check that its code matches this one (type it in if it isn't filled in), then approve. This page continues automatically.

risk.title: Know the risk before you sign in
risk.text: This signs in through the login Google built for {{tool}}, not one Google offers for mu. Google may consider this a violation of its terms and limit or suspend your account.
risk.instead: Use an account you can afford to lose access to. The official options are a Gemini API key or Vertex AI with a gcloud sign-in.

commands.frame: Show the task frame: the goal, your constraints with their source, the current subgoal and the acceptance criteria
commands.remember: Save a lesson for later work in this project: /remember <what to do>
commands.lessons: List this project's lessons (id · kind · recalled/followed · lesson); /lessons all adds global and retired lessons
commands.forget: Retire a lesson so it's no longer recalled: /forget <id prefix> (find IDs with /lessons)
commands.capabilities: Show what's installed and what's turned on; /capabilities open <id> turns one on
commands.permissions: Set how much mu can do without asking: /permissions full | judge | ask (no argument opens a picker); /permissions reset clears what you've allowed so far
commands.lsp: Show the language servers: what's installed, what's running and the last error
commands.goal: Keep the agent working until a condition holds: /goal <condition> sets it, /goal shows it (or asks for one), /goal clear ends it
commands.board: Show the plain-language board; /board on|off turns it on or off for this project, /board model picks the model that writes it
commands.checkpoints: List the checkpoints so far: turn, time and the files changed since each
commands.rewind: Go back to a checkpoint: /rewind [#] [both|files|conversation]; /rewind undo reverses the last rewind
commands.swarm: Show what each subagent is doing; /swarm stop [name] asks it to report now, /swarm kill [name] stops it immediately
commands.agents: List the subagent roles the delegate tool can use, and where to add your own
commands.hive: Have several investigators work on one question at once: /hive <question>. With no question, it works like /swarm
commands.browse: Have the built-in browser open a page and do what you ask: /browse <url> [goal]
commands.inherit: Show what mu inherited from Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, and from which files
commands.mcp: Manage MCP servers: sign in, reconnect, enable or disable, and change exposure
commands.jobs: List background jobs; /jobs stop <id|all> stops them
commands.commit: Split uncommitted changes into commits: shows the plan, commits only when you approve and never pushes
commands.review: Have the reviewer subagent review uncommitted changes, or whatever you name; the judge ranks findings from P0 to P3
commands.mu: Show mu's status. Also: /mu judge <judges> | /mu route <point> <judge|default> | /mu mode <point|default> <off|shadow|active>
commands.status: Show the model, the judge, each decision point's mode, context savings and recent verdicts
commands.help: Show what mu can do and the commands worth knowing
commands.ledger: Show the last n verdicts and their latency: /ledger [n]
commands.doctor: Check that the judge, model, browser and subagents are set up
commands.import-chat: Import a Claude Code or Codex conversation from this project and continue it here: /import-chat [file]

native.compacted: Conversation compacted here to free up space: {{tokens}} tokens of earlier messages were summarized.
native.compactedPlain: Conversation compacted here to free up space.
native.forkNoEntry: the message has no session entry yet

status.classifying: The judge is reading your message…

send.placeholderWorking: Steer mu now, or queue a message for when it's done…
send.steerHint: Reaches mu at its next step

dialog.countdown: Closes in {{seconds}}s, then mu continues without your answer.

host.restartHint: Send a message to start mu again.

error.off: The native host is off (MU_NATIVE_HOST=0). Restart the app without that setting to use it.
error.noHarness: The app can't find mu to run.
error.oldHarness: This version of mu is too old to run in the app. Update mu, then try again.
error.plan: The app couldn't work out how to start mu.
error.noModels: mu stopped: it has no model to use.
error.failed: mu stopped before it could start.
error.closed: mu was closed for this conversation.
error.noFolder: The project folder no longer exists, so mu can't start there.
error.invalid: The app sent a request mu couldn't read.

empty.title: New conversation in {{folder}}
empty.body: mu works in this folder. Tell it what you want done.

sider.title: Recent
sider.deleteConfirm: Delete "{{title}}"? Its file moves to the trash, so you can still restore it.

notify.failed: A run stopped with an error

panel.noLessons: Lessons appear once the conversation opens.

source.label: Changes in {{folder}}
source.noGit: Git couldn't run here, so changes can't be shown.

home.noFolder: Choose a folder for mu to work in first.

details.lead: Each feature has one switch, with its settings under Options. Indented rows are the feature's decision points, where it asks the judge. Turn one off and that step runs as usual.

skills.lead: The skills mu can use in every conversation, and where each comes from.
skills.added: Added {{name}}. New conversations can use it.
skills.removeContent: Its folder moves to the trash, and new conversations won't load it.
skills.project: Project skills (.mu/skills, .agents/skills, .claude/skills) load only in that project's conversations and aren't listed here.

mu.title: mu's skills
mu.help: In {{folder}}. Skills you add go here, and only these can be removed.

agents.title: Shared skills
agents.help: In ~/.agents/skills, shared by several agents. mu reads them but never changes them.

builtin.title: Built-in
builtin.help: Shipped with mu. Each one is available while the feature it belongs to is on.

claude.title: From Claude Code
claude.help: From ~/.claude/skills. mu only reads them; turn off features.inherit in mu.json to stop using them.

codex.title: From Codex
codex.help: From ~/.codex/skills. mu only reads them; turn off features.inherit in mu.json to stop using them.

mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.lead: The MCP servers mu can use in every conversation, and where each is set up.
mcp.added: Added {{name}}. New conversations can use it.
mcp.empty: mu isn't using any MCP servers yet.
mcp.featureOff: The MCP feature is off in mu.json: only the servers in mcp.json are used.
mcp.unreadable: Couldn't read these files, so their servers are missing: {{files}}
mcp.project: Project servers (.mu/mcp.json, .mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json) are used only in that project's conversations and aren't listed here.

offInSource.label: Off in its source
offInSource.help: It's turned off in its own tool's settings. mu doesn't change other tools' files, so turn it on there.

unsupported.label: Not supported
unsupported.help: It uses the legacy HTTP+SSE transport, which mu doesn't support.

mu.title: mu's servers
mu.help: In mcp.json and mu.json. Servers you add go into {{file}}, the same as with mu mcp add.

claude.title: From Claude Code
claude.help: From ~/.claude.json. Turning one off here only writes to mu.json, never to Claude Code's file.

cursor.title: From Cursor
cursor.help: From ~/.cursor/mcp.json. Turning one off here only writes to mu.json, never to Cursor's file.

codex.title: From Codex
codex.help: From ~/.codex/config.toml. Turning one off here only writes to mu.json, never to Codex's file.
